question: People tasted the same minced beef labelled either 75% lean or 25% fat. How did the label affect ratings after eating?
options: No difference once they had tasted it
answer: Rated better when labelled 75% lean. It was judged leaner, higher in quality and less greasy, and the effect shrank but did not vanish after tasting. Both labels state the same fact; one draws the eye to the meat, the other to the fat. The tongue followed the label.
move: Restate any figure in its opposite terms before judging it.
ask: What claim did I accept recently that would have felt different stated the other way round?
trap: No difference once tasted: the mouth should overrule a label.
source: Levin & Gaeth, Journal of Consumer Research, 1988
reference: Levin & Gaeth, How consumers are affected by the framing of attribute information before and after consuming the product, Journal of Consumer Research, 1988
